toc.title: The Problem: AI Agents Acting Without Empirical Grounding
toc.purpose: Establish urgency—AI agents are increasingly deployed in economic decisions, yet the industry lacks real-stakes testbeds to study emergent behaviors (collusion, manipulation, incentive hacking), creating blind spots for learner-AI interaction design and governance.
subpoints: Growing AI agent adoption in education and enterprise (Gartner 40%+ by 2026; Deloitte 25%→50%)
Existing research relies on synthetic rewards with limited external validity (ABIDES-Economist, LLM Economist, AI Economist)
Cost of inaction: delayed understanding of failure modes undermines SGE's learner-centered evaluation work and Sony Group's governance stance
Why this matters now: first-mover advantage in defining research benchmarks; competitors may set standards first

toc.title: The Proposal: AI Agent Economy Competition
toc.purpose: Describe what is being proposed—a controlled on-chain testbed where AI agents transact under real incentives, generating auditable datasets and institution-design frameworks.
subpoints: Competition format: humans submit agents pre-launch; agents autonomously transact on a private chain; on-chain logs enable reproducibility
Research outputs: auditable datasets, institution-design frameworks, publications
Key design principles: human-in-the-loop rule design, explicit governance boundaries, learner-centered evaluation alignment
What is out of scope: building participant agents, mainnet deployment, long-term commitments beyond pilot

toc.title: Proof: Credibility and Differentiation
toc.purpose: Build confidence that the proposal is credible and differentiated from alternatives.
subpoints: Nyx Foundation track record: 17 vulnerabilities reported in Ethereum Fusaka audit (#1 by report count)
Participation benchmarks: Google ADK Hackathon (10,400+ participants, 477 projects); ARC Prize ($1M) as prize benchmark
Differentiation from alternatives: auditable on-chain logs vs opaque corporate sandboxes; real incentives vs synthetic-reward simulations
Alignment with SGE's blockchain credential work (2017 learning-record system) and Startale/Soneium trust-infrastructure mission

toc.title: Feasibility and Fit
toc.purpose: Demonstrate operational viability and strategic alignment across Sony Group, SGE, and Startale/Soneium.
subpoints: Modular participation tiers minimize burden: observer → advisor → co-designer → sponsor
Private chain + sandbox isolation + kill-switches address security and integrity concerns
September 2025 target is internal and adjustable; pilot phase validates feasibility before any large commitment
Strategic synergy: research outputs inform SGE's AI-in-education roadmap; trust-infrastructure positioning for Startale/Soneium
Operating model clarity: Nyx Foundation owns operations unless jointly agreed; each entity designates one owner

toc.title: Risk Handling and Governance
toc.purpose: Directly counter likely objections and demonstrate that risks are managed, not ignored.
subpoints: Brand/regulatory safety: private chain with no public token, no speculation; brand/legal review gates built into phased approach
Data governance: human-in-the-loop rule design, access control for datasets, explicit disclosure policy
Security controls: sandbox isolation, kill-switches, multi-validator enforcement, external audit plan before September 2025
Emergent harmful behaviors become research data, not uncontrolled risk (post-hoc analysis framework)
Exit gates: each phase has explicit exit criteria if value not demonstrated

toc.title: Investment, ROI, and Decision Request
toc.purpose: Frame the low-commitment entry, strategic returns, and specific next steps.
subpoints: Low-commitment entry: exploratory meeting costs only time; no budget commitment until pilot scope agreed
Strategic returns: reusable research assets (datasets, frameworks, publications); positioning at AI-agent frontier; talent pipeline via participation
Cost structure overview: 16M JPY prize pool (internal notes); platform/ops costs to be defined in scoping phase
Decision request: approve cross-entity exploratory meeting within 4 weeks; designate one owner per entity; align on 2-3 research questions each entity wants answered
Next step: 30-60 minute workshop agenda with decision tree and exit ramps

argument_tree.root: A cross-entity exploratory meeting should be approved within 4 weeks to assess whether co-sponsoring or co-designing the AI Agent Economy Competition—a controlled on-chain testbed studying AI behavior under real incentives—can generate reusable research assets (auditable datasets, institution-design frameworks) that inform SGE's AI-in-education roadmap, Startale/Soneium's trust-infrastructure positioning, and Sony Group's frontier AI governance stance, with participation tiers (observer to co-designer) enabling low-commitment entry and clear exit gates.

branches.claim: Current pain: The industry lacks empirical testbeds to study how AI agents behave under real economic incentives; most simulations use synthetic rewards, limiting generalizability and leaving emergent risks (collusion, manipulation) poorly understood.
because: Existing agent-economy research (ABIDES-Economist, LLM Economist, AI Economist) uses synthetic environments without meaningful stakes
Lack of auditable, reproducible execution logs limits third-party verification and research validity
Enterprise AI agent adoption is accelerating (Gartner 40%+ by 2026; Deloitte 25%→50%), making empirical grounding urgent
evidence: ABIDES-Economist (arXiv 2024-03-10): multi-agent economic simulation with synthetic rewards
LLM Economist (OpenReview): multi-agent economic simulation with LLM-based agents, synthetic environment
AI Economist (Salesforce): multi-agent economic simulation for policy design, no real-stakes incentives
Gartner forecast: 40%+ of enterprise apps embed conversational AI by 2026 (press release 2024-04-01)
Deloitte forecast: AI agents adoption from 25% (2025) to 50% (2027) (press release 2024-12-05)

branches.claim: Solution validity: A private-chain competition with auditable logs, human-in-the-loop rule design, and explicit governance boundaries uniquely combines incentive realism, reproducibility, and safety controls—directly aligned with SGE's learner-centered evaluation priorities and Startale/Soneium's trust-infrastructure mission.
because: Private blockchain provides tamper-resistant logs enabling reproducibility and third-party verification
Competition format with prize money creates meaningful stakes that reveal more realistic behaviors
Human-in-the-loop rule design and explicit governance boundaries address algorithmic dominance concerns
Alignment with SGE's stated priorities: real-time, multi-dimensional, learner-centered evaluation (Isozu 2025 interview)
evidence: Sony/SGE blockchain for education data (2017): tamper-resistant registration and access control
Isozu interview (2025-06-11): AI era shifts from memorization to evaluating information; AI agents may handle 'teach & assess' while humans focus on facilitation
Prize competition benchmark: Google ADK Hackathon (10,400+ participants, 477 projects)
Prize benchmark: ARC Prize ($1M Grand Prize); Netflix Prize ($1M, historical reference)

branches.claim: Feasibility: Nyx Foundation has demonstrated Ethereum security credibility (17 vulnerabilities reported in Fusaka audit, #1 by report count); modular participation tiers and staged pilot phases minimize operational burden for each entity; September 2025 target is internal and adjustable.
because: Nyx Foundation's Fusaka audit performance demonstrates blockchain security expertise
Modular tiers (observer → advisor → co-designer → sponsor) allow low-commitment entry
Staged approach with pilot phase validates feasibility before large commitments
Each entity can participate at their comfort level and exit at defined gates
evidence: Nyx Foundation Fusaka audit: 17 vulnerabilities reported, #1 by report count (PR TIMES 2025-12-24; contest window 2025-09-15 to 2025-10-13)
Participation tiers defined in proposal: observer, advisor, co-designer, sponsor
Phase structure: Design & Sponsor Alignment → Pilot → Public Competition → Post-Competition Research
Exit criteria defined per phase in proposal plan

branches.claim: Risk handling: Private chain (no public token, no speculation), sandbox isolation with kill-switches, brand/legal review gates, and post-hoc analysis of harmful behaviors convert risk into research data—not uncontrolled exposure.
because: Private chain avoids regulatory/brand risks associated with public tokens and speculation
Sandbox isolation and kill-switches contain agent misbehavior and enable safe termination
Brand/legal review gates at each phase ensure governance sign-off before progression
Emergent harmful behaviors (collusion, manipulation) become valuable research data through post-hoc analysis
evidence: Private chain design: authenticated agent-only TX, no mainnet deployment
Security controls: sandbox isolation, rate limits, multi-validator checks, kill-switches (per proposal feasibility)
Risk register includes: exploitation attempts, platform instability, manipulation/collusion, legal/regulatory uncertainty—each with mitigation
External audit plan: timeline and scope for third-party review before September 2025
